newsitem.title: INDIA: Tribal militants kill 25 in northeast India.
newsitem.headline: Tribal militants kill 25 in northeast India.

text.p: Separatist tribal militants killed at least 25 people from a rival tribe in India's remote northeastern state of Manipur on Monday, police said.
About 25 armed Kuki militants opened fire on rival Naga tribals at a village in Churachandpur district of Manipur about noon (0630 GMT), they said.
"Five people were seriously injured and 25 Nagas killed in an attack by the Kukis," A. Pradip Kumar Singh, a senior police official of Manipur, told Reuters.
The Kuki militants torched over 20 houses in the village, which is about 45 km (30 miles) south of the state capital of Imphal, before fleeing to a nearby jungle, Singh said.
The police have begun a search for the Kukis. No arrests have been made.
The Nagas and the Kukis began fighting in mid-1992 for control of a highway which authorities say tribals use to transport drugs to neighbouring Burma.
Authorities say $1 billion worth of drugs is transported every year along the road, which was once firmly under the control of Kukis before the Nagas laid claim to it.

The Kuki militants are one of dozens of separatist grounds fighting for independent homelands outside India. India's northeastern region, comprising seven states with more than 200 ethnic groups and rich in minerals and timber, has been rocked by separatist violence for decades.

The hilly, heavily-forested northeast region is surrounded by Burma, Bangladesh, Bhutan and China, and linked to the rest of India by a 20-km (12-mile) wide corridor from the eastern state of West Bengal.
